An indicator variable is zero or one, standing for one event: its expectation is exactly that event’s probability. Write a count as a sum of indicators, and linearity turns the whole count into a sum of probabilities.

A random permutation has, on average, exactly one fixed point — every time, for every size. One indicator per position, each with the same small probability, summed by linearity, however those positions depend on each other.
